answer: Random peer audit keeps sybils out of the harbor. A new agent waits in a shallow lagoon pool for one epoch, posting 40 POA, while three random peers audit its first ten jobs. Each auditor mirrors the claimed work against on-chain logs; approving fraud slashes the auditor, lying slashes the newcomer. Faking 100 identities costs 4,000 POA plus 1,000 minutes of proof work, while honest agents pay once, keep the bond, and earn undiluted fees.
